feat: Add storage profile-level credential control flags (#1518)

* feat: Add storage profile-level credential control flags

Add profile-specific flags to control vended credentials and remote signing:
- S3Profile: Add remote_signing_enabled (sts_enabled already exists)
- AdlsProfile: Add sas_enabled for SAS token control
- GcsProfile: Add sts_enabled for downscoped tokens

All flags default to true for backward compatibility via serde defaults.

Add new TableConfigError variants:
- VendedCredentialsDisabled: HTTP 403 when vended credentials disabled
- RemoteSigningDisabled: HTTP 403 when remote signing disabled

This implements the profile-level approach requested in PR #1511 review,
replacing warehouse-level flags with provider-specific controls.

Part 1/3: Storage profile fields and logic

* feat: Add S3 signer remote signing check

Add remote_signing_enabled check to S3 signer endpoint handler:
- Verify S3Profile.remote_signing_enabled before processing sign requests
- Return HTTP 403 Forbidden if remote signing is disabled
- Return HTTP 400 Bad Request if storage is not S3

This completes the profile-level enforcement of credential flags.

Part 2/3: Handler updates

* feat: Add storage profile-level credential control flags

Adds per-storage-profile flags to control vended credentials and remote
signing, replacing the previous warehouse-level implementation.

Changes:
- S3Profile: Added `remote_signing_enabled` field (default: true)
- AdlsProfile: Added `sas_enabled` field (default: true)
- GcsProfile: Added `sts_enabled` field (default: true)

Implementation:
- All fields use serde defaults for backward compatibility with existing
  JSONB-stored profiles
- Added validation in credential generation: returns HTTP 403 when
  disabled
- Added validation in S3 remote signing handler
- Updated all test helpers and profile instantiations
- Updated error handling with VendedCredentialsDisabled and
  RemoteSigningDisabled variants

Documentation:
- Added entries to storage.md configuration parameter tables for all
  three storage types

Backward compatibility:
- No database migration needed (JSONB + serde defaults handle this)
- Existing profiles without these fields will default to enabled (true)
- Clean implementation at storage profile level as requested by
  maintainer

Resolves feedback from PR #1511 review

* chore: Run cargo fmt

* docs: Regenerate management OpenAPI spec

Update management-open-api.yaml to include new storage profile credential control flags:
- S3: remote-signing-enabled
- Azure: sas-enabled
- GCS: sts-enabled

* fix: Wire ADLS/GCS credential flags into validate_access

Previously, validate_access() always attempted to validate vended credentials
for ADLS and GCS profiles, even when sas_enabled/sts_enabled were set to false.
This caused warehouse creation to fail with VendedCredentialsDisabled error.

Now the validation correctly skips vended credential checks when the flags
are disabled, while still validating direct read/write access. This aligns
ADLS/GCS behavior with S3, which already respects sts_enabled during validation.

Fixes CodeRabbit nitpick comment on PR #1518.

feat(role): reserve `system` provider for catalog-managed roles (#1776)

* feat(role): reserve `system` provider for catalog-managed roles

Introduces a `system` role-provider namespace alongside the existing
`lakekeeper` one. The catalog seeds these per project; the role-
management API rejects any request that targets `system`, and they
cannot be created, updated, or deleted from outside.

Downstream binaries (e.g. lakekeeper-plus) declare the actual role
list by passing a `Vec<SystemRoleSpec>` into `serve()` and
`run_post_migration_hooks()`. The spec list is installed into a
process-wide registry which the catalog reads when creating a new
project (seeding) and when running the post-migration backfill
(adding system roles to pre-existing projects). The OSS binary
passes an empty vec — no behavior change.

Catalog-side mechanics:
  * `RoleProviderId::lakekeeper()` / `is_lakekeeper()` /
    `is_system()` predicates replace the previous string checks.
  * `create_roles_impl` takes an `OnRoleConflict` mode; seeding uses
    `UpdateMetadata` (idempotent name/description refresh via
    `ON CONFLICT (project_id, provider_id, source_id) DO UPDATE
     ... WHERE IS DISTINCT FROM`).
  * `delete_roles_impl` generalised to take
    `CatalogListRolesByIdFilter` so downstream extensions can
    deprecate retired system roles via the trait — no raw SQL.
  * No schema change: role names remain unique per project
    (case-insensitive). Downstream seeders must pick collision-
    resistant names; collisions surface as `RoleNameAlreadyExists`.

Cedar/OpenFGA/role-cache/assignment paths are unchanged — they all
key on `RoleId` or `(provider_id, source_id)`, never on name.

fix(postgres/migrations): rewrite namespace trigger so pg_restore can replay it (#1781)

The `set_updated_at_and_increment_version` trigger on `namespace` was
created in 20251027163724 with `WHEN (OLD IS DISTINCT FROM NEW)`.
20260219081950 later added the STORED generated column `namespace.depth`,
and Postgres bans whole-row OLD/NEW references in BEFORE-trigger WHEN
clauses on tables with generated columns at CREATE TRIGGER time. The
live trigger keeps working on the source DB — PG validates at trigger
creation, not at runtime — so sqlx migrations succeed and UPDATEs run
fine. The failure surfaces only on pg_dump → pg_restore: pg_dump emits
the trigger in canonical `(old.* IS DISTINCT FROM new.*)` form and
pg_restore refuses to re-create it against the rebuilt schema, which
by then already has `depth`. Reported by a customer migrating their
Postgres backend to a new instance.

Replace the WHEN clause with an explicit column list. Semantics
preserved: meaningful UPDATEs bump version/updated_at, no-op UPDATEs
don't. The migration is a `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` + `CREATE TRIGGER`
so it's idempotent and converges fresh installs and already-broken DBs
to the same safe form. `project` and `warehouse` carry the same trigger
pattern but have no generated columns, so they aren't affected today
and are left untouched.

Two new tests guard against regression. `test_no_wholerow_before_trigger
_on_generated_column_tables` is a cheap SQL introspection check for the
exact pattern. `test_pg_restore_round_trip_then_crud` snapshots every
trigger's `pg_get_triggerdef()` output (the same DDL pg_dump emits),
drops and re-executes it against the post-migration schema — the step
that fails in a real pg_restore — then drives namespace, table, and
view CRUD through the catalog API. Both fail on main without the fix.

Roles carry a provider namespace in their identity (`provider~source_id`).
Roles resolved from a configured role provider (LDAP/Entra/Okta/token) are
maintained by provider sync, so mutating them through the management API
creates drift the next sync silently clobbers.

reports the provider namespaces owned by a configured role provider, plus a
guard `reject_managed_provider` (renamed from `reject_system_provider`) that

writable. Enforcement is API-layer, matching `SystemRoleImmutable`.

OSS, AllowAll and OpenFGA are unaffected. The enterprise Cedar authorizer
populates the set (separate change). No migration.

fix: limit connection lifetimes (#1990) (#1993)

Four independent causes of RSS growing until restart:

- Transparent huge pages defeat jemalloc's page release: it frees at 4 KiB
  granularity, but a 2 MiB huge page cannot be partially freed, so one live
  page keeps all 2 MiB resident. Forces thp:never via both the build variable
  and an exported malloc_conf symbol, since either can be lost silently.
  AnonHugePages 286 MiB -> 0, settled RSS -68%, throughput +1.9%.

- axum::serve rebuilt the whole route table per accepted connection
  (Router::with_state), holding the copy for the connection's lifetime:
  ~1 KiB of live heap per route per connection, ~370 KiB here before any
  request. into_make_service drops it to ~3.6 KiB at equal throughput.

- hyper's per-connection read buffer grows to 408 KiB and never shrinks, and
  nothing set TCP keepalive or a header-read timer, so connections whose peer
  vanished were held for the life of the process. Per-connection cost after a
  1 MiB request: ~464 KiB -> ~86 KiB.

- Unmatched request paths became permanent Prometheus series (~1.9 KiB of
  live heap each, never reclaimed) because axum-prometheus falls back to the
  raw URI when there is no MatchedPath.

Also adds jemalloc gauges, which separate a real leak (allocated grows) from
allocator retention (resident grows, allocated flat) from THP-trapped pages
(both look fine, RSS climbs); normalizes the forwarded prefix in the UI asset
cache key; and skips the cloud-event publisher when no sinks are configured.

Behaviour changes:
- Idle HTTP/1 connections close after 75s (nginx's keepalive_timeout). A
  client taking a pooled connection at the boundary must retry.
- The 64 KiB buffer ceiling also caps the request head; larger heads get 431.
- Shutdown drains for at most 10s.
- The idle timeout and buffer cap are HTTP/1 only.
- Unmatched paths now report endpoint="unmatched"; dashboards grouping by raw
  path lose that data.

* fix(server): expose open connection count as a metric

tokio_live_tasks_count counts every task on the runtime, so it cannot
distinguish many open connections from a task leak elsewhere. The accept loop
now tracks connections directly, making live_tasks minus
lakekeeper_http_connections the leak signal.

Declares socket2's "all" feature, which gates TcpKeepalive::with_retries. It
was previously reachable only because an unrelated dependency chain happened
to enable it, so the accept loop would have stopped compiling if that chain
changed.

Makes test_index_prefix assert the behaviour the running configuration
selects, rather than depending on LAKEKEEPER__USE_X_FORWARDED_HEADERS, and
records on ServeConfiguration::cloud_event_sinks that the publisher is
registered only when it is non-empty.

fix(catalog): return 409, not 404, when a rename target is taken (#1955)

The spec enumerates renameTable's 404 as exactly two cases — source table
missing, target namespace missing — and 409 for "already exists as a table
or view". We returned 404 on a collision, telling the client the source had
vanished. A soft-deleted name also blocked the rename, though create reuses
such names freely.

Both came from the conflict_check CTE, which turns out to re-implement the
unique_name_per_namespace_id index: same key, same case-insensitive
collation, no extra predicates. Drop it and map the constraint violation to
TabularAlreadyExists instead. deleted_at is in the index key and the renamed
row is always live, so soft-deleted namesakes stop blocking by construction,
and the concurrent-insert race that used to 500 now takes the same path —
FOR UPDATE locked existing rows but could not block an insert.

A conflict now aborts the caller's transaction, as any constraint violation
does. All three callers propagate it; create_tabular already works this way.

fix(s3): don't vend a credential-less `storage-credentials` entry (#1923)

* fix(s3): don't vend a credential-less `storage-credentials` entry

For S3 warehouses, `region`, `endpoint`, `path-style-access` and the SSE-KMS
properties were mirrored into the credential-refresh properties before the
vending branch ran. That map is what every caller checks to decide whether to
emit a `storage-credentials` entry, so warehouses that vend nothing — STS
disabled, and not Cloudflare R2 or Alibaba Cloud OSS — still returned an entry
scoped to the table prefix carrying no credential at all.

Clients that honour access delegation (DuckDB's iceberg extension requests it
by default) build a key-less, prefix-scoped secret from that entry and then send
unsigned requests for every file below the table prefix, which the storage
rejects with 403 — while the credentials the client already had would have
worked. Files fetched outside that scope still succeeded, so the failure looked
intermittent and file-specific. Independent of `remote-signing-enabled`: the
remote-signing properties travel in the load config, not in the credentials.

Clear the credential-refresh properties when nothing was vended, document the
"non-empty means a credential was vended" invariant on `TableConfig::creds`, and
route the five call sites through a single `TableConfig::storage_credentials`.

Closes #1920

fix(s3): sign ListObjectsV2 for prefixes inside a table location (#1925)

The signer rejected bucket-level ListObjectsV2, so any Iceberg client
walking a prefix through S3FileIO failed - concretely Spark's
`remove_orphan_files` with `prefix_listing => true`, the only route for
remote-signing users. The parser allowed a keyless bucket path for
DeleteObjects only, and the location was derived from the URI path,
never from the `prefix` that identifies the table.

Listing is now signable when `prefix` addresses a directory inside the
table location. Sigv4 covers the query string, so the signed prefix
cannot be widened afterwards. The prefix must reach past the table's
path separator: S3 matches prefixes as raw strings, so
`warehouse/ns/table` would also return the keys of a sibling
`warehouse/ns/table_other`. Adds `Location::is_prefix_within`, since
`is_sublocation_of` accepts the parent itself.

The URI is signed as received and S3 dispatches on both path and query,
so bucket-level requests must not address a key (this also hardens the
pre-existing DeleteObjects path), and only ListObjectsV2 parameters are
accepted, each at most once. Requests carrying no prefix (`?versions`,
`?uploads`, `?location`, List Objects V1) stay unsignable.

fix(api): mark responses private and vary on the request identity (#1947)

Catalog and management responses are principal-specific — bodies are
filtered by the caller's permissions and loadTable may embed vended
storage credentials — but carried no cache directives, so a shared cache
could store and heuristically reuse one (RFC 9111 4.2.2).

`Vary: authorization, x-project-id, x-iceberg-access-delegation` on the
catalog, management and lakekeeper nests. Applied as router layers, so
200, 304 and error responses are all covered; /health is mounted after
and stays unaffected.

Not `no-store`: that would forbid client-side storage and make
If-None-Match revalidation unreachable. `private` closes the shared-cache
hole while leaving the ETag mechanism intact. `if_not_present`, so the S3
signer keeps its stricter `private, no-cache`.

fix(catalog): advertise idempotency-key-lifetime as a top-level field (#1952)

The spec defines idempotency-key-lifetime as a sibling of
overrides/defaults on CatalogConfig, and its presence is the only signal
that the server supports Idempotency-Key. We put it in the overrides
map, so RESTSessionCatalog's null check never fired and the Java client
silently disabled idempotency against a server that fully implements it.
The feature has worked since 0.13.0; it was invisible.

Emitting it top-level also routes it into java.time.Duration.parse,
which rejects the weeks designator — so a P7D lifetime, previously an
opaque string in overrides, would now fail the entire config response
and kill RESTCatalog.initialize(). Advertise via a formatter that never
produces P<n>W. The shared formatter keeps the weeks form, which other
Lakekeeper APIs emit.

Extract the enabled/disabled mapping so it is testable without a
database: the disabled path had no coverage, and advertising a lifetime
the server won't honor is the inverse of the signal clients need.
